bull_bear.body: Debt-free status maintained. Strategy: 60-70% of operating cash flow allocated to capex for 20%+ CAGR growth; 30% retained for incremental working capital. Minimum cash balance of INR 500-600 cr maintained on balance sheet for liquidity buffer.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Supply chain volatility (XLPE imports from Middle East disrupted); Shipping logistics constraints impacting export timing; Raw material price volatility (though hedged by pass-through); Execution risk on Sanand Phase 2 timeline; Geopolitical tensions affecting export routes.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Bullish on domestic infrastructure capex (Power T&D, Railways, Data Centers). Confident in volume guidance despite Q4 logistics noise. Pragmatic on margins (conservative 10.5-11% guide) but highlights operating leverage potential. Transparent about dealer churn (10-12%) and capacity constraints.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Dealer network depth: Top 5% of dealers contribute 70-80% of B2C sales, while the long tail (2,000+ dealers) serves rural/retail wire demand with high churn. Working capital cycle improving (2.97 months vs 3.39 months) due to channel financing, allowing debt-free growth despite expanding scale. EPC business intentionally capped at 2-3% of revenue to avoid working capital drag.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Very low leverage: Total Debt (including discounting arrangements from banks) of 1,342 (FY24), 1,783 (FY25), 1,862 (FY26) INR Mn against Net Worth of 31,483 / 57,858 / 66,650; the balance sheet shows nil non-current borrowings across Q1 FY27, FY26 and FY25.
- Credit rating of AA+ (stable) long term and A1+ short term, with a "Track record of Consistent Debt Servicing" and "Insurance of Receivables to Mitigate risk".
- Equity raised via QIP is still being deployed — footnotes state return ratios are computed on "Average Capital Employed, excluding unutilized QIP proceeds" and that "ROE lower due to Increased Net Worth from QIP Proceeds for FY 25 & FY 26"; reported ROCE was 27% / 25% / 24% and ROE 20% / 16% / 15% for FY24 / FY25 / FY26.
- Cash and Bank Balances of 19,153 (FY25), 15,126 (FY26) and 10,540 (Q1 FY27) INR Mn alongside rising Net Fixed Assets, i.e. cash being channelled into capacity rather than distributed — the deck states no dividend or buyback policy.
- Shareholding as of 30th June 2026: Promoters 35.00%, FII 27.32%, DII 25.90%, Public/Other 11.78%; total institutional holding 53.22%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: B2C (Dealer) sales INR 1,936 cr (+29% YoY, 56% mix); Domestic Institutional Cable INR 804 cr (+6%); EHV Cable INR 188 cr (+64% YoY); Exports INR 443 cr (constrained by logistics); EPC (non-cable) INR 123 cr. Full Year FY26: Net Sales INR 11,746 cr (+20.7%), Wire & Cable value +22.3%.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain disruption for XLPE from Middle East and high freight costs | Polycab India | beneficiary | Med | If KEI faces prolonged logistics issues in Middle East exports, competitors with diversified shipping lines may gain share, though KEI's domestic strength mitigates this. |
| Surge in Data Center and Power T&D capex requiring specialized EHV cables | KEI Industries | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of Sanand capacity coming online just as demand from data centers and grid modernization peaks; EHV order book grew 64% YoY. |
| Volatility in copper prices impacting working capital for smaller players | Unorganized Cable Manufacturers | loser | High | KEI's pass-through mechanism and strong balance sheet allow it to thrive, while smaller unorganized players struggle with cash flow and pricing power. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "One of the leading manufacturers of cables and wires with a wide product portfolio spread across EHV, HT and LT Power Cables, House Wire, Stainless Steel Wire", and "Forward integrated into EPC services for Power, Distribution, Transmission and sub-station projects".
- Scale markers on the Overview slide: 9 manufacturing plants across Rajasthan, Gujarat and D&NH; 2,200+ employees (as on 31st March 2026); 2,100+ dealers/distributors (as on June 2026); 2,000+ institutional customers (as on 31st March 2026).
- Healthy order book of INR 42,919 Mn as on July 2026, described as "Healthy Order Book to achieve Turnover and Profitability".
- Low customer concentration: "top 10 customers accounting for 13% of sales in FY26 and 15% in Q1 FY27"; deck states "Diversification helps in de-risking".
- Exports: "Presence in 60+ countries with offices in 4 countries" (UAE, South Africa, Nepal, Gambia); exports also described as a "natural hedge on forex (given we also import raw materials)".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Industry] CRISIL MI&A-sourced view that the India wires & cables market grows at an 11-13% CAGR between FY24-29E, from INR 859 Bn (FY19) to 1,702 Bn (FY24) to ~INR 3,000 Bn (FY29E, midpoint of an INR 2,865-3,135 Bn range); power transmission cables (28-30%) and building wires (21-23%) are ~50% of the market.
- [Industry-Exports] Share of exports in the overall Indian wires & cables market rose from 5% in FY19 to 10% in FY24 and is expected to grow at a 10-11% CAGR over FY24-29E; India aspires to lift its share of the global export pie from ~1% to almost 3% by 2034, with the deck flagging Indian product as "10-20% more expensive vs China now".
- [Brand] IPL sponsorship from FY17 to FY26 plus Pro Kabaddi jersey sponsorships; Super Brand Status for FY 2011-16 and FY 2019-26; Advertisement & Publicity expenses of INR 405 Mn (FY24), 478 Mn (FY25), 539 Mn (FY26).
- [CSR] CSR spend of INR 101 Mn (FY24), 129 Mn (FY25), 158 Mn (FY26), centred on the "Swasthya Utsav" health programme for electricians and their families including free health check-ups and ABHA card creation.
- [Management] Promoter-led board with Mr. Anil Gupta as Chairman-cum-Managing Director, Mr. Akshit Diviaj Gupta as Whole Time Director and Mr. Rajeev Gupta as Executive Director (Finance) & CFO; separate SVP-Operations heads for the Bhiwadi, Silvassa and Sanand plant clusters.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded to 12.21% in Q4 despite freight headwinds. Raw material (Copper +16.85%, Aluminum +9.91% avg FY26) fully passed through via tender pricing mechanism. Freight costs to Middle East up significantly in April, but 50% borne by customers; forex gains (INR 90-91/$) offsetting remaining impact.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 20%+ CAGR expected (volume 17-18% + price pass-through); Margin: 10.5%-11% (conservative), potential for 50 bps expansion via scale in FY28; Order Inflow: Strong visibility in EHV and Data Centers; Capex: INR 600-700 cr annually for next 2-3 years.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Total visible: INR 3,585 cr as of Mar 31, 2026. Breakup: EPC (INR 309 cr), EHV Power Cable (INR 625 cr), Domestic Institutional Cable (INR 2,154 cr), Export Cable (INR 497 cr). Additional L1 pending for EHV: INR 233 cr. Dealer orders (fast-moving) excluded from this figure.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Sanand Plant Phase 1 commissioned Dec '25 driving FY27 volume; Phase 2 expected Q4 FY27 driving FY28 volume (another 17-18% growth). US market re-entry targeting 20% export mix. Backward integration into medium voltage compounds (2-year timeline) and galvanized steel wire armor.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: KEI Industries delivered strong Q4FY26 results with 19% revenue growth and margin expansion to 12.2%, driven by robust B2C demand and a 64% surge in EHV cable sales. The core narrative shifts to FY27 where the commissioning of the Sanand plant phases promises 17-18% volume growth, potentially unlocking 25%+ top-line growth if copper prices remain elevated, while the company successfully navigates supply chain disruptions to re-enter the US market.

open.item: Ad spend of approximately INR75-80 cr in this financial year (FY26).
Sanand second and last phase (EHV) expected to be commissioned in Q4 FY27 (by March 2027); ~INR385 cr unutilized QIP money to be fully deployed in FY27.
Company expects to take exports to around 20% of total sales in FY27, having restarted US exports after the tariff lull.
EHV segment expected to grow around 20% in FY27, mostly from existing (near-full) capacity plus some from Sanand.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected on a conservative basis around 10.5% to 11%.
With 17-18% volume plus metal price inflation, FY27 value growth will be more than 20% (potentially ~25-30% if copper prices sustain/rise).
Company expects 17% to 18% volume growth in FY27, mainly from the Sanand new facility (cables) and Chinchpada (wire).
By FY27, with capacities normalized, company could do roughly INR13,500 cr turnover with exports around INR2,000 cr or more.
open.promised: 13500 cr turnover; 2000 cr exports INR cr

open.item: In FY27-28, when Sanand reaches full capacity, EBITDA margin will improve by another ~0.5% (plus 20-25 bps per year from scale/export/B2C mix).
FY28 growth expected around 20% as Sanand capacity keeps ramping and stabilizing (another 17-18% volume growth from Phase 2).
Net working capital cycle to remain ~85-90 days; receivables reduced to 1.88 months and may fall to 1.75 months; overall inventory+debtor-creditor ~2.97 months.
Company will fund all future capex from internal accruals (~60-70% of accrual to capex, 30% to working capital) and remain debt-free for the next 4-5 years at 20% CAGR.
Dealer/distribution contribution expected to remain at 53% to 55% of overall sales.
EPC business (2.6% of FY26 revenue) will be kept at only 2-3% as a supporting business for EHV cable projects.
Company will set up in-house manufacture of medium-voltage compounds (min 2 years) and its own galvanized steel/cable armor wire (~5,000 tonnes/month consumption).
Company will do ~INR600-700 cr capital expenditure each year for the next 2 to 3 years (may include Bhiwadi), funded from internal accruals.
US export order book was ~INR50-60 cr at 31 Mar 2026; company aims to reach ~INR40 cr/month (prior peak) within ~3 months as the market reopens post-tariff.
Management flags new wire entrants (Torrent, Surya, Roshni, Luker, Bajaj etc.) but expects limited impact as brand/network build takes 4-7 years; outsourcing model unlikely to work.
Company is working on solar and wind power tie-up agreements (15-20 year) expected to conclude in the next 2 to 3 months to reduce power cost.
Company will remain focused on wire and cable business and does not intend to diversify into other solar item chains.
